analysis: The PR is documentation-only: docs/reference/protocol-messages.md changes the date stamp (line 3) and clarifies the sample_age_ms semantics (base line 578, head lines 578-584). Age is now measured from the newest observation, even if an older completed observation arrives later. A new paragraph says the Swift producer (EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift) applies the same rule to each workload bucket and current-posture series. It also says the EWMA and sample counts keep receipt order, and wire fields are unchanged. No auth, attestation, encryption, billing, or routing control is changed, and no wire shape changes. The affected data is capacity and performance telemetry. The protocol doc itself says this is diagnostic or advisory and does not authorize admission, routing or prefix reuse. Providers are adversarial and could misreport sample age, but that risk existed before this PR. The coordinator's freshness handling (reconcileCapacitySamples, capacity_sample_freshness.go) was not supplied, so I could not check that the documented newest-observation age semantics match the code. This is a documentation-accuracy question and not a security regression. No threat-model update is needed: the T-041 cache and other retained entries are untouched, and the unit texts show base content only, with changes visible via the patch. Further review would only need to confirm the Swift producer matches the doc.
